nodes.name: ZnO NRs/NF fabrication
nodes.procedure: The NF was first ultrasonically vibrated with acetone, followed by a treatment with 3 M HCl and ethanol. Subsequently, it was soaked for 60 min in a nucleation solution containing 0.005 M Zn(CH3COO)2 and 70 mL ethanol. The treated NF was then heated in air at 300 °C for 10 min, with a heating rate of 3 °C/min. Following the heating process, the NF was cooled to room temperature. Subsequently, 45 mL of the reaction solution containing 0.025 M Zn(NO3)2 and 0.025 M HMTA was stirred on a magnetic stirrer. Then, 1.8 mL of 33% NH3 solution was gradually added to the reaction solution. The mixture was stirred for 30 min before being transferred to a Teflon flask. The NF is positioned along the wall of the Teflon jar. The reaction vessel is then placed in a reactor at 90 °C for 4 h, with a heating rate of 3 °C/min. After the reaction, the Zn(OH)2/NF was thoroughly washed several times with ethanol and deionized water, followed by drying at 70 °C for 5 h. Finally, the Zn(OH)2 was calcined at 300 °C for 3 h, with a heating rate of 3 °C/min, yielding ZnO NRs/NF after cooling to room temperature.
nodes.source_text: 2.2. Fabrication of ZnO nanorods on nickel foam ... yielding ZnO NRs/NF after cooling to room temperature.

nodes.name: W-NiO/Cr2S3 electrodeposition and etching
nodes.procedure: A 50 mL reactant solution was prepared by mixing 5 mM NiCl2, 40 mM Na2WO4, 10 mM CrCl3, and 0.4 M thiourea. Then, a working electrode consisting of ZnO NRs/NF (1×1 cm) was prepared. An Ag/AgCl reference electrode and a graphite rod counter electrode were set up in the reactant solution. The electrodeposition process was performed at a voltage of -1.1 V for a duration of 4500 s (75 min), this resulted in the deposition W-doped NiO/Cr2S3 on the ZnO NR/NF substrate. After the electrodeposition, the sample was thoroughly washed with deionized water several times. Then, the sample was dried in an oven at 70 °C and annealed at 300 °C for 1 h. The sample was soaked in a 30% NH4OH solution for 3 h to effectively remove ZnO. The process described above was repeated to synthesize W-NiO, W-Cr2S3, and NiO/Cr2S3 on NF, individually, in the absence of precursors containing Cr-S, Ni, and W, respectively.
nodes.source_text: 2.3. Synthesis of W-NiO/Cr2S3, W-NiO, W-Cr2S3 and NiO/Cr2S3 on nickel foam ... The process described above was repeated to synthesize W-NiO, W-Cr2S3, and NiO/Cr2S3 on NF

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms NiO (JCPDS 04-0835) and rhombohedral Cr2S3 (JCPDS 01-072-1224) phases in tube W-NiO/Cr2S3 after ZnO removal; no distinct W phase peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of tube W·NiO/Cr2S3 does not exhibit specific diffraction peaks representative of the W phase. ... the diffraction peaks of W·NiO/Cr2S3 can be indexed to the NiO pattern (JCPDS No. 04–0835) and the crystal of Cr2S3 in the rhombohedral phase (JCPDS No. 01–072–1224).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Cr2S3 Eg mode at 290 cm⁻¹, Ag modes at 187.0 and 342.1 cm⁻¹, NiO mode at 550 cm⁻¹; W-doping reduces peak intensity and causes shifts indicating lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distinct Raman peak observed at 290 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the in-plane Eg mode, while the peaks at 187.0 and 342.1 cm⁻¹ represent the characteristic Ag mode of Cr2S3. ... Raman bands observed at 550 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to NiO modes.

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption shows tube W-NiO/Cr2S3 BET surface area of 124.7 m²/g with mesopores 3.0-6.5 nm; tube NiO/Cr2S3 shows 133.5 m²/g with micropores 2-4.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1h, the surface area of tube NiO/Cr2S3 is measured at 133.5 m² g⁻¹. ... these tube W/NiO/Cr2S3 is 124.7 m² g⁻¹ and range of pore size from 3.0 to 6.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms elemental composition of tube W-NiO/Cr2S3: W 1.3%, Ni 25.7%, Cr 2.8%, S 2%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of W was confirmed through inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES), with W content measured at 1.3%, Ni at 25.7%, Cr at 2.8%, and S (2%), respectively, in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Ni²⁺ (Ni 2p 855.2/872.7 eV shifted 0.5 eV lower), Cr³⁺/Cr⁶⁺ (Cr 2p 576.6/585.9 eV and 577.9/587.4 eV), S²⁻ (S 2p 161.9/168.0 eV), W⁶⁺ (W 4f 34.8/36.9 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3b displays the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum of NiO/Cr2S3, where four peaks are observed. The peaks at 855.6 and 873.1 eV correspond to Ni²⁺ ... In the case of W·NiO/Cr2S3, two peaks at approximately 855.2 and 872.7 eV can also be attributed to Ni²⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in 0.92-1.02 V vs RHE at 5-50 mV/s scan rates yields double-layer capacitance Cdl = 9 mF cm⁻² for tube W-NiO/Cr2S3/NF, indicating highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cyclic voltammetry measurements of the composites were conducted over a potential range of 0.92–1.02 V, referenced to a reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), at different scanning speeds ranging from 5 to 50 mV s⁻¹. ... Fig. 6b displays that the W-NiO/Cr2S3 nanotube exhibits the largest Cdl values (9 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy at 0.01-10⁵ Hz shows charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.44 Ω for tube W-NiO/Cr2S3/NF, lowest among tested catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy was performed at a frequency range of 0.01-10⁵ Hz. ... tube W·NiO/Cr2S3 exhibited the lowest charge transfer resistance value (Rct = 0.44 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS color mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni, O, W, Cr, S elements throughout tube W-NiO/Cr2S3 nanotube structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images in Fig. 2g and Fig. S10, along with their corresponding EDS color mapping images, confirm the well-distributed presence of W throughout the NiO/Cr2S3 structure.
